label: conj:six-term-per-derivation-weights
title: Per-derivation weights for the six-term mass formula
html:
The atomic binding energy is assembled from the six terms, with energy scales E_{0,\beta} (the β-decay scale), \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G (13.2.15) and m_e:

\begin{aligned}
  B(Z, N) \;=\;&
  \underbrace{E_{0,\beta} \cdot \big(T_1^{\rm free} - T_1^{\rm atom}\big)}_{\text{T1 binding}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\alpha \cdot \big((T_2 + T_3)^{\rm atom} - (T_2 + T_3)^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T2/T3 binding}}
  \\[2pt]
  &+\;
  \underbrace{m_e \cdot \big(T_4^{\rm atom} - T_4^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T4 binding}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{E_{0,\beta} \cdot (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1^{\rm atom}}_{\text{T5 binding}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\big(T_6^{\rm atom} - T_6^{\rm free}\big)}_{\text{T6 binding}}
\end{aligned}

The scale difference separating T_1 from T_2+T_3 isolates the weak scale from the hadronic core.

Comparison boundary. No derived value of E_{0,\beta} is on record. The numerical evaluation sets it to the measured free-neutron β-decay Q-value (the CAL-2 proxy), and takes the free-particle baseline Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z\,m_e from CODATA. Those inputs belong to the comparison with AME binding energies, not to the assembly stated above.
